name: Shanaz Hemmati
profile: Iranian-born, UT Austin-trained engineer who co-founded Austin-based ZenBusiness with Ross Buhrdorf (2015 per company); the small-business formation/AI platform has helped 700,000+ entrepreneurs and was valued at ~$1.7B after a $205M Series C. Long-time COO, she is now Co-Founder & Executive Advisor; earlier led tech at Excite.com and HomeAway.
interesting_fact: She left Iran as a child to study in the U.S.; at ZenBusiness she led a DEI strategy reaching nearly 50% female representation across staff and management, and was named to Inc.'s 2025 Female Founders list.
deep_cut_fact: She was inducted as a 2026 Distinguished Alumna of UT Austin's Electrical & Computer Engineering department; she met co-founder Ross Buhrdorf years earlier when both worked at Excite.com.
notes: Founding year given as 2015 (company) vs 2017 (Entrepreneur). She is a Capital Factory mentor in Austin; also appeared on Startergirlz podcast. Route via ZenBusiness press.

name: Ed Thompson
profile: British software engineer who co-founded Manchester-born data-integration company Matillion with CEO Matthew Scullion in 2011. He led the team that launched Matillion ETL in 2014; the cloud data pipeline company (now pushing its 'Maia' agentic data team) raised $150M Series E at a $1.5B valuation in 2021 and reached ~$2B in later rankings.
interesting_fact: Matillion is one of the few UK tech unicorns founded in Manchester; it later built a major second hub in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: Before Matillion he spent 11 years as an IBM software consultant to UK blue-chip companies; Matillion ran for three years before he and his team shipped the flagship ETL product in 2014.
notes: Common name; identity tied to Matillion CTO. Writes bylines for DBTA, DevOps.com, Solutions Review; appeared on 'Data Sharks' podcast. Route via Matillion press.

name: Philip Kaplan
current_role: Founder, DistroKid; also makes small-batch headphones (Pud's Small Batch Headphones)
profile: Philip 'Pud' Kaplan (b. 1975) is a serial internet entrepreneur: dot-com-era satirist (Fucked Company, 2000), founder of ad network AdBrite (2004), creator of TinyLetter (sold to Mailchimp 2011) and of Fandalism, which became DistroKid in 2013. DistroKid, the flat-fee music distributor he calls the biggest in the world, was valued around $1.3B after a 2021 Insight Partners investment.
interesting_fact: Since 2024 he has gone viral on Reddit building wild novelty headphones (Helmholtz resonators, wine-cork damping, a built-in CD player, a water-pump 'rain' pair) that he sells in tiny batches from pud.com.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a children's picture book about audio, 'Music Production ABCs', published by DistroKid, and is a drummer in the death-metal side project Butchers of the Final Frontier.
notes: Very online and approachable via X (@pud) and his headphone site; Syracuse iSchool '97, gave its 2014 convocation address. DistroKid valuation detail per press reports (Insight Partners 2021).

name: Wagde Zabit
profile: Israeli software engineer from Kafr Manda in the Galilee and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (2019), the agentless cloud-security (CNAPP) company valued at $1.8B in 2021. A Technion computer-science graduate, he left a long engineering career at Check Point to co-found Orca, where he remains a hands-on senior engineer.
interesting_fact: He is one of the very few Arab-Israeli co-founders of an Israeli cybersecurity unicorn; Calcalist profiled him as 'the entrepreneur from Kafr Manda who built a cybersecurity unicorn'.
deep_cut_fact: At age five his father, a math teacher turned computer instructor, gave him a Commodore 64 - the first computer in Kafr Manda - and he was programming in BASIC and Logo by first and second grade.
notes: Low public profile; an engineer rather than spokesperson (CEO Gil Geron and CTO Avi Shua front the company). Recent releases also route media via Inkhouse agency. Best route: Orca press.

name: Leng Jing (冷静)
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Mengxiang Technology (梦饷科技, formerly Aikucun / 爱库存); Vice President, China Association of Trade in Services
profile: Shanghai e-commerce executive who co-founded Aikucun in 2017 with founder/chairman Wang Min; the inventory-clearance social-commerce platform rebranded as Mengxiang Group in 2020 and raised a C round that made it a unicorn. Its B2R2C model lets millions of mostly female 'shopkeepers' resell brand stock via mini-stores; she now pitches it as a 'dual SaaS' channel for China's industrial-belt brands.
interesting_fact: By 2021 Mengxiang said it had helped 2M+ shopkeepers, 95.5% of them women (many stay-at-home mothers), earn nearly RMB 5B in income; she frames the business as creating flexible jobs for women.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Aikucun she was VP and partner at the Chinese e-commerce consultancy Zhengwang Consulting (正望咨询) and VP of Tmall service partner Ruijinlin's e-commerce and Yunxiang Digital units.
notes: Hurun lists her as founder; company records name Wang Min as founder/chairman and Leng Jing as co-founder/CEO. Gave a keynote at the June 2026 Cross-Border E-commerce Development Conference (yzwb.net). No published press email found; approach via Mengxiang corporate PR.
